target.title: fix(cron): preserve one-shot reschedules during active runs
target.body:
Closes #111383

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators rescheduling an active one-shot cron job would lose the future invocation when the original run completed. A successful `deleteAfterRun` job was deleted, while a retained one-shot was disabled, even though its schedule had moved into the future.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron completion now compares the admitted job's normalized scheduling inputs with the current stored row. When an in-flight edit owns a different schedule, the completed run still records its run and delivery metadata but cannot delete, disable, retry, advance, or disarm the edited schedule. The same ownership rule covers scheduled and manual runs.

## User Impact

Operators and agents can reschedule a running one-shot job without the completed invocation silently removing or disabling the new future run. The future schedule remains durable across Gateway restart.

## Evidence

- Regression first reproduced on current `main`: `deleteAfterRun=true` removed the job; `deleteAfterRun=false` left it disabled with no `nextRunAtMs`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.read-ops-nonblocking.test.ts`: 6/6 passed, including both delete policies, restart persistence, and the manual-run sibling path.
- `pnpm test:changed -- src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/ops.ts src/cron/service.read-ops-nonblocking.test.ts`: 57/57 passed.
- Expanded cron proof (`schedule-identity`, `service.read-ops-nonblocking`, `ops.run-admission`, `ops.regression`, `timer.regression`, `service.trigger-eval`): 131/131 passed.
- Hosted CI exposed an `on-exit` schedule-identity gap in the first revision. The follow-up adds normalized identity for its command and working directory; the exact failing regression and the broader 131-test cron suite now pass locally.
- Isolated Gateway proof on Node 24.15.0: a real command payload wrote `started-2`, ran for 30 seconds, and was rescheduled by CLI to `+5m` while `status=running`. After it wrote `done-2`, `cron list` showed the same job with `enabled=true`, the future `at` timestamp, `lastStatus=ok`, and `lastDurationMs=30034`. The same state survived a clean Gateway restart.
- `pnpm check:changed -- ...`: formatting, repository guards, plugin boundaries, and core typecheck passed. The local core-test typecheck was interrupted after 846 seconds without diagnostics; hosted CI remains the authoritative full typecheck.
- Full `pnpm build` reached `tsdown-unified` but the host had only 114 MiB free and failed with `ENOSPC`; source CLI builds completed successfully and powered the live Gateway proof.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex helped implement and validate this change; I reviewed the diff and understand the code.
